title: Cap. 1 prol. IV: against Pelagian merits and scholastic merita congrua
pass_a_gloss: For when they dispute against the Pelagians that grace is not given or denied according to the merits of free choice, they mean nothing other than that it is not given according to a foresight condition of the good or bad use of that same free choice. For if the Pelagians had proven this, the Fathers would never have denied that it is a true cause of conferred grace. So also when our Theologians contend against some Scholastics that God does not predestine humans from foresight congruent merits, they mean nothing other than that these things called congruent merits are not antecedent and distinguishing conditions according to which all in whom those were foresight are elected, and all in whom they were not are rejected. For if they have demonstrated that such are conditions, the Scholastics have the matter finished, and we of our own accord will confess that they are causes of the discrimination of the elect and the reprobate, in that sense in which the vocabulary of cause and merit is used. Key lemmas: Pelagiani; merita congrua; Scholastici; Theologi nostri.
pass_b_english: When the Fathers argue against the Pelagians that grace is not given or withheld according to free choice's merits, they mean simply this: it is not given according to a foresight condition of free choice's good or bad use. Had the Pelagians proved that, the Fathers would never have denied it was a true cause of the grace conferred. So too when our theologians contend against some Scholastics that God does not predestine people from foresight congruent merits, they mean that these so-called congruent merits are not antecedent distinguishing conditions by which everyone in whom they were foresight is elected and everyone in whom they were not is rejected. If the Scholastics ever prove such conditions, their case is finished — and we will freely admit that those conditions are causes of the divide between elect and reprobate, in the sense in which cause and merit are spoken of.
source_text: Nam quando contra Pelagianos disputant, gratiam non dari aut negari secundum merita liberi arbitrii, nihil aliud volunt, quam non dari secundum praevisam conditionem boni aut mali usus ejusdem liberi arbitrii. Si enim Pelagiani hoc evicissent, Patres nunquam negassent esse veram causam gratiae collatae. Sic etiam cum Theologi nostri contra Scholasticos nonnullos contendunt, Deum non praedestinare homines ex praevisis meritis congruis, nihil aliud volunt, quam haec quae appellantur merita congrua non esse conditiones antecedentes ac distinguentes, secundum quas eligantur omnes in quibus illae praevisae fuerant, rejiciantur omnes in quibus non fuerant. Nam si tales conditiones esse demonstraverint, rem confectam habent Scholastici, & nos ultro fatebimur esse causas discriminis electorum & reprobatorum, eo sensu quo causae & meriti vocabulum usurpatur.
